free_tier.stated: A Startup Allocation may request up to 20,000 node-hours annually, a Research Allocation has a maximum size of 100,000 node-hours annually, and an Educational Allocation may request up to 10,000 node-hours. 'Allocations are provided through NSF funding at no direct cost to the end user to anyone who meets the eligibility criteria above.' 'Startup and Educational Allocation requests receive a fast track review, bypassing the Allocation Advisory Board' and 'DesignSafe project staff will review these requests according to the merit review criteria above, and will act on these requests within two weeks of their submission.' 'Startup Allocations may be for unfunded exploratory research'. 'Users who are not eligible for an NSF-provided allocation, may choose to purchase additional compute time or storage capacity from TACC' at rates of 'approximately $60/TB/year' for storage and 'approximately $0.50 per node hour' for compute as of January 2024.

notes: The account is open to anyone, but the account alone does not reach the HPC queue: portal tools are capped by "built-in constraints that limit the amount of compute time" with no published ceiling, and command-line access needs the allocation. Startup review skips the Allocation Advisory Board and is decided within two weeks, which makes 20,000 node-hours the realistic ask rather than the 100,000. The no-cost extension reported in the July 2025 council message is a horizon fact: the corpus should re-check this record when that extension ends rather than treating the allocation as permanent. The corpus holds no DesignSafe record. Node-hour to core-hour conversion depends on the TACC system assigned, which the page does not name, so no conversion is published here.
